solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Substitute $x=u^2$, $dx=2u\,du$: $\int\frac{2u}{u^2+u}du=\int\frac2{u+1}du=2\ln|u+1|+C=2\ln(\sqrt x+1)+C$.

**Answer: $2\ln(\sqrt x+1)+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=x^2$, $du=2x\,dx$: the integral is $2\int_0^\infty\frac{du}{1+u^2}=2\cdot\frac\pi2=\pi$.

**Answer: $\pi$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $x=\sec\theta$, $dx=\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta$, $\sqrt{x^2-1}=\tan\theta$: the integral becomes $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sec\theta\tan\theta}{\sec^2\theta\tan\theta}d\theta=\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos\theta\,d\theta=1$.

**Answer: 1**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Integrate $\ln(1+\frac1x)$ by parts: $\int\ln(1+\tfrac1x)dx=x\ln(1+\tfrac1x)+\int\frac{x}{x(x+1)}dx=x\ln(1+\tfrac1x)+\ln(x+1)$. So an antiderivative of the integrand is $x\ln(1+\frac1x)$. At $\infty$ it tends to $1$ and at $x=1$ it is $\ln2$. The value is $1-\ln2$.

**Answer: $1-\ln2$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac{\sin^4\theta}{\cos\theta}=\frac{(1-\cos^2\theta)^2}{\cos\theta}=\sec\theta-2\cos\theta+\cos^3\theta$, and $\cos^3\theta=\cos\theta(1-\sin^2\theta)$. Integrating: $\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|-2\sin\theta+\sin\theta-\frac{\sin^3\theta}3+C$.

**Answer: $-\frac{\sin^3\theta}{3}-\sin\theta+\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
An antiderivative is $2x-\sqrt{x^2+\pi^2}-\sqrt{x^2+e^2}$. As $x\to\infty$, $x-\sqrt{x^2+a^2}\to0$, so the value at $\infty$ is $0$. At $x=0$ it is $-\pi-e$. The integral is $0-(-\pi-e)=e+\pi$.

**Answer: $e+\pi$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
For $x\ge0$: $\sin(\tan^{-1}\sqrt x)=\frac{\sqrt x}{\sqrt{x+1}}$, so the integrand is $\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}}$. On $[-1,0)$, with principal branches $\sqrt x=i\sqrt{|x|}$ and $\sin(\tan^{-1}(is))=\frac{is}{\sqrt{1-s^2}}$, the product is again the real function $\frac{x}{\sqrt{x+1}}$ throughout $[-1,8]$.

With $u=x+1$: $\int_0^9\frac{u-1}{\sqrt u}du=\left[\frac23u^{3/2}-2\sqrt u\right]_0^9=18-6=12$.

**Answer: 12**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
$\frac{\sin2x}{1+\cos x}=\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{1+\cos x}$. With $c=\cos x$, $dc=-\sin x\,dx$: $-2\int\frac{c}{1+c}dc=-2(c-\ln|1+c|)+C$. (Equivalently $2(\ln|\csc x+\cot x|-\ln|\csc x|-\cos x)+C$.)

**Answer: $2\ln(1+\cos x)-2\cos x+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
The denominator is $x(x+\ln x)$ and $\frac{d}{dx}(x+\ln x)=\frac{x+1}x$, so the integrand is $\frac{(x+\ln x)'}{x+\ln x}$. Hence the integral is $\ln|x+\ln x|+C$.

**Answer: $\ln|x+\ln x|+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $y(x)$ be the nested radical. Pulling out $x$ shows $y=\sqrt{1+xy}$, i.e. $y^2-xy-1=0$, so $x=\frac{y^2-1}y=y-\frac1y$. At $x=0$, $y=1$; at $x=\frac32$, $y=2$.

Then $\int_0^{3/2}y\,dx=\big[xy\big]-\int_1^2x\,dy=3-\int_1^2\left(y-\frac1y\right)dy=3-\left(\frac32-\ln2\right)=\frac32+\ln2$.

**Answer: $\frac32+\ln2$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=\frac1{x+u}$, so $u^2+xu-1=0$ and $u=\frac{\sqrt{x^2+4}-x}2$. Then
$$\int_0^{3/2}u\,dx=\frac12\left[\frac x2\sqrt{x^2+4}+2\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2+4}\right)-\frac{x^2}2\right]_0^{3/2}.$$
At $x=\frac32$: $\sqrt{x^2+4}=\frac52$, giving $\frac{15}8+2\ln4-\frac98$; at $0$: $2\ln2$. So the value is $\frac12\left(\frac34+2\ln2\right)=\frac38+\ln2$.

**Answer: $\frac38+\ln2$**

reviewNote: Official key says 16 ln 2 + 3, but numerical integration gives 1.0681 = 3/8 + ln 2; stored the verified value.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Write $6+6\cos^2x=12-6\sin^2x=-2(1+3\sin^2x)+14$. So the integrand is $-2+\frac{14}{1+3\sin^2x}$. Using $\int_0^\pi\frac{dx}{1+3\sin^2x}=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{1\cdot4}}=\frac\pi2$, the integral is $-2\pi+14\cdot\frac\pi2=5\pi$.

**Answer: $5\pi$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
In the second term let $x=u^3$: $\int_0^1\sqrt{x+\sqrt[3]x}\,dx=\int_0^13u^2\sqrt{u^3+u}\,du$. Adding the first term (in the variable $x$): $\int_0^1(3x^2+1)\sqrt{x+x^3}\,dx=\left[\frac23(x+x^3)^{3/2}\right]_0^1=\frac23\cdot2\sqrt2=\frac{4\sqrt2}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{4\sqrt2}{3}$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Since $\sec^2x=1+\tan^2x$, the sum telescopes: with $t=\tan^2x$, $\sum_{n\ge2}\left(\frac1{\sqrt{n-1-t}}-\frac1{\sqrt{n-t}}\right)=\frac1{\sqrt{1-t}}$. So the integral is $\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-\tan^2x}}$. With $u=\tan x$: $\int_0^1\frac{du}{(1+u^2)\sqrt{1-u^2}}$; with $u=\sin\theta$: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{d\theta}{1+\sin^2\theta}=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sec^2\theta}{1+2\tan^2\theta}d\theta=\frac\pi{2\sqrt2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi}{2\sqrt2}$**

prompt: Evaluate $\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\frac{4\log^2\left(\csc^2x\right)}{\tan x}\,dx$. (Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.)

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $u=\sin^2x$, $du=2\sin x\cos x\,dx$, so $\frac{dx}{\tan x}=\frac{du}{2u}$, and $\log(\csc^2x)=-\ln u$. The integral is $\int_{1/2}^1\frac{2\ln^2u}{u}du=\frac23\left[\ln^3u\right]_{1/2}^1=\frac23\ln^32$.

**Answer: $\frac23\ln^32$**

reviewNote: Official key says log^2(2), which is the value if the integrand had log (not log squared). As printed, log^2(csc^2 x) gives (2/3)ln^3 2 (natural log). If log means log base 2, the value is (2/3)ln 2, accepted as an alternative.

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Since $\cos3x=4\cos^3x-3\cos x=\cos^3x-3\sin^2x\cos x$, the integral is $\int e^{17x}\cos3x\,dx=\operatorname{Re}\int e^{(17+3i)x}dx=\operatorname{Re}\frac{e^{(17+3i)x}}{17+3i}=\frac{e^{17x}(17\cos3x+3\sin3x)}{17^2+3^2}$, and $17^2+3^2=298$.

**Answer: $\frac{e^{17x}(17\cos3x+3\sin3x)}{298}+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Note $\frac1{\sqrt{x^2+1}}=e^{-\frac12\ln(x^2+1)}$, so the integrand is $e^{g(x)}\tan^{-1}x$ with $g(x)=x\tan^{-1}x-\frac12\ln(x^2+1)$. Then $g'(x)=\tan^{-1}x+\frac x{1+x^2}-\frac x{x^2+1}=\tan^{-1}x$, so the integrand is $\frac d{dx}e^{g(x)}$.

**Answer: $\frac{e^{x\tan^{-1}x}}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Since $\frac{d}{dx}\left(x^2e^{x-1/x}\right)=\left(2x+x^2\left(1+\frac1{x^2}\right)\right)e^{x-1/x}=(x+1)^2e^{x-1/x}$, the integral is $\left[x^2e^{x-1/x}\right]_0^\varphi=\varphi^2e^{\varphi-1/\varphi}-0=\varphi^2e$, because $\varphi-\frac1\varphi=1$ and $x^2e^{-1/x}\to0$ as $x\to0^+$. Also $\varphi^2=\varphi+1=\frac{3+\sqrt5}2$.

**Answer: $\varphi^2e$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Differentiate $\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{x^3}$ by the quotient rule: $\frac{\frac{x^3}{x^2+1}-3x^2\tan^{-1}x}{x^6}=\frac1{x^3(x^2+1)}-\frac{3\tan^{-1}x}{x^4}=\frac1{x^5+x^3}-\frac{3\tan^{-1}x}{x^4}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{x^3}+C$**

solutions.title: Solution
solutions.body:
Let $I$ be the integral and substitute $x\mapsto\frac\pi4-x$: $\tan(\frac\pi4-x)=\frac{1-t}{1+t}$ ($t=\tan x$), so $1+\tan(\frac\pi4-x)=\frac2{1+t}$ and $I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{\sqrt{1+t}}{\sqrt[4]2\sqrt{1+t}+\sqrt2}dx=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{\sqrt{1+t}/\sqrt[4]2}{\sqrt{1+t}+\sqrt[4]2}dx$. Adding the two forms: $2I=\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{1+\sqrt{1+t}/\sqrt[4]2}{\sqrt[4]2+\sqrt{1+t}}dx=\frac1{\sqrt[4]2}\cdot\frac\pi4$. Hence $I=\frac{\pi}{8\sqrt[4]2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\pi}{8\sqrt[4]2}$**
